title: Fight in Faith
summary: We didn't save ourselves, and our own strength won't carry us to the finish. A faithful God will complete what he started.
exhortation: We did not save ourselves. We couldn't, and we didn't even want to. We were saved by the grace of Jesus Christ, by his blood shed on the cross, by his righteousness exchanged for our sin and shame. So we can't expect that after we're saved, our own strength will get us across the finish line. We need to look to Christ: what he has done and what he is doing.

We depend on a faithful God. All through Scripture we see his faithfulness: despite our sin, despite our mistakes, despite what's done to us, God is faithful through it all. That is what will bring to completion the work he started in us. And we depend on a God who gave himself for us. He didn't leave us to figure it out. He came and sacrificed himself on our behalf.

We know this. But these are the things we need to remind ourselves of every morning, because our flesh, our pride and our selfishness are at war against them. It's not that we don't know them. It's that we don't walk in them. So when we wake up, it's good to rehearse the gospel and remember what will bring us faithfully to the end: the faithfulness, mercy and grace of our God.

And that is what gives us confidence to fight to walk in these truths. With Paul we can say, "One thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus." Let's run in faith today and fight in faith today, because God is with us and he is faithful.
prayer: Lord, remind us of your completed work this morning. As we charge into our day, as we work and play, train our children and talk with friends, be front and center in our minds. Lift our eyes to you, Jesus, so we remember that your work is complete.

It is the only confidence we can have before a holy God: your righteous work is done. When you said it was finished, it was truly and completely finished. Every prophecy fulfilled, the righteous life lived, your blood poured out, the wrath of God absorbed. The work is done. Lord, may we live in it. Amen.
